overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding its November 17 joint meeting with the Council without posting notice; the Council, and the Board on the complaint-discussion issue, did not violate the Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to sufficiently discuss a November 5 Open Meeting Law complaint at its November 17 meeting, voting instead to refer it to counsel.
allegations.key_passage: We have previously explained that referring a complaint to legal counsel rather than discussing its substance is permissible, and we therefore find that neither the Board nor the Council violated the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly failed to sufficiently discuss an October 27 Open Meeting Law complaint at its November 17 meeting, voting instead to refer it to counsel.
allegations.key_passage: We have previously explained that referring a complaint to legal counsel rather than discussing its substance is permissible, and we therefore find that neither the Board nor the Council violated the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly held a joint meeting with the Council on November 17 without posting notice for that joint session.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board failed to post notice of its November 17 joint meeting with the Council 48 hours in advance of the meeting, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly held a joint meeting with the Board on November 17 without posting notice for the joint portion.
allegations.key_passage: On the other hand, we find that the Council properly posted notice of its November 17 meeting in accordance with G.L. c. 30A, § 20(b) and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to announce the name of each member participating remotely at a December 16 meeting; the complainant later withdrew this allegation.
allegations.key_passage: after we addressed a similar issue, and found no violation, in OML 2020-168.

remedy: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
